summary: No computation, no Lean. Corrected NULL-TRANSFER.md on four points. (1) H ('every finite set translates into the domain') is SUFFICIENT, NOT NECESSARY: the exact criterion is chi(R^2) <= chi(C\Z) iff every finite unit-distance graph embeds in the graph on C\Z; H is a checkable stronger condition. Z = C, k = 1 shows only that SOME hypothesis is needed. (2) A HALF-PLANE DOES satisfy H, so my half-plane counterclaim was false; replaced by the positive statement that a proper 6-colouring of a half-plane would also give chi(R^2) <= 6. A fixed-width strip need not satisfy H: larger-diameter graphs do not fit. (3) An arbitrary colouring of all cell interiors need not be cell-constant; cell-constancy is now an explicit hypothesis of the Cayley-graph equivalence. (4) Compactness is USED, not proven indispensable to all proofs; the only device tried (one global translate) needs Z empty. Accepted no-go interval stated as (1/sqrt28, 1/sqrt12) only; the old extension through 1/2 is under audit and unused. k-generic extraction: exists_properColoring_of_finset (Converse.lean:33) is fully k-generic; finite_config_proper (Converse.lean:13) too but needs Measurable + WeakColoring, so wrong tool; in not_proper_five_coloring_compl_null (NullSetRobust.lean:20) the translation block is k-generic and the Fin 5 dependence is ONE line (Five.lean:133).

verified_results.statement: Correction 1: (H) is sufficient but not necessary. Exact criterion: chi(R^2) <= chi(C\Z) iff every finite unit-distance graph embeds as a subgraph of the unit-distance graph on C\Z (forward by de Bruijn-Erdos, chi(R^2) = sup over finite graphs). (H) implies this embeddability by isometric translation and is strictly stronger.
verified_results.grade: PROOF (my own reasoning this block); supersedes the withdrawn necessity claim

verified_results.statement: Correction 2: a closed half-plane satisfies (H) (translate far along the inward normal), so a proper 6-colouring of a half-plane would also give chi(R^2) <= 6. A fixed-width strip need not satisfy (H): a unit-distance graph of diameter exceeding the width cannot be translated into it. The earlier half-plane counterclaim is retracted.
verified_results.grade: PROOF; retraction of my earlier false claim

verified_results.statement: Correction 3: an arbitrary colouring of C\B need not be constant on any cell interior; the Cayley-graph equivalence (cell-constant colouring iff strict forced-pair separation, with diam(C) <= 1) requires cell-constancy as an EXPLICIT hypothesis. The transfer lemma itself never uses cell structure.

Correction 4: compactness (Tychonoff/de Bruijn-Erdos) is USED in the short proof and is not removable there, since the finite characterisation is the only device used to uniformise over finite sets; but its indispensability to every possible proof is NOT claimed.

Correction 5: the accepted no-go interval is (1/sqrt28, 1/sqrt12) = (0.188982, 0.288675) only, the union of the two certified patches at a = 1/5 and a = 1/4. The older extension of the exclusion through a = 1/2 (from the T^2-clique argument on (1/sqrt13, 1/2]) is under audit and is not used in NULL-TRANSFER.md.

Source extraction, compactness step: exists_properColoring_of_finset at Converse.lean:33 is fully k-generic ({k : Nat} [NeZero k], hypothesis over Finset C, conclusion ProperColoring k), using Pi.compactSpace and a finite-intersection argument on the closed sets t p. No Fin 5 appears.

conjectures: Because a half-plane satisfies H, the transfer lemma is not about thinness; the sharp question for a domain D is whether every finite unit-distance graph embeds in it, and for a strip of width w that fails exactly when a unit-edge chain longer than w/sqrt(1-w^2 /4) exists. Whether the half-plane case is strictly easier than the plane is open and not addressed here.
A k-generic formalisation is mechanical rather than mathematical (one line changes); the only real risk is simp behaviour around Fin k in the hzero/hpos step.
